analyst.summary: IIFL Capital Services had a soft FY26 on the bottom line, with profit down 21% even as revenue was about flat, largely reflecting an industry-wide squeeze on retail stock-broking revenue after regulatory changes reduced derivatives trading volumes across all Indian brokers. The company's investment-banking and institutional-equities business had a strong year, finishing as India's #1 IPO bookrunner by deal count, which is helping offset the retail-broking headwind. The stock is not expensively priced. We rate it a Hold: real near-term profit pressure from an industry-wide cause, balanced by a genuinely strong and growing investment-banking franchise.
